target.name: RobCo
target.founder: Roman Hölzl, Paul Maroldt, Constantin Dresel

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $1.4B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
RobCo is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Roman Hölzl, Paul Maroldt, and Constantin Dresel, having raised $160M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 9 private robotics firms (including Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics) and 1 public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The Stage-Progression method, using $1.4B as a proxy for total capital deployed, applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A advancement to subsequent rounds, implying a $2.7B valuation. The Peer-Median method examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B (Series B), Dexterity at $1.6B (Series B), and Walden Robotics at $1.1B (Seed). The resulting peer median is $1.6B, with a range of $1.1B to $1.8B.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.4B (low) to $3.1B (high), with a median of $2.2B. The Stage-Progression method yields the upper bound, reflecting forward-looking growth assumptions; the Peer-Median approach anchors the lower end, emphasizing current-stage comparability. Key uncertainties include the timing and size of the next financing event, as well as execution risk relative to stage-equivalent peers. The wide range reflects tension between capital-intensity justifications and peer-based benchmarking in an early-stage, capital-hungry sector.
